history.summary: CSV NAME FLAG: the CSV row name 'Ashtabujakaram (Ulagalantha Perumal) Temple' conflates two distinct Divya Desams. Ashtabujakaram is a separate temple (the 44th Divya Desam in standard lists) whose moolavar is Adikesava Perumal, also called Gajendra Varadar and Ashta Bhuja Perumal - the eight-armed form of Vishnu. The Ulagalantha Perumal Temple complex is a different site (housing the Tiruooragam, Tiruneeragam, Tirukkaragam and Tirukkaravanam Divya Desams) already covered by seq 975 (id ulagalantha-perumal-temple-kanchipuram) in this dataset. This record documents Ashtabujakaram, in Chinna Kanchipuram about 2 km from the Varadaraja Perumal Temple. Legend: when Brahma performed his yajna, Saraswati tried to disrupt it, finally sending a ferocious sarpam (serpent); Vishnu appeared with eight arms holding eight weapons and killed it - the serpent is represented as Sarabesan in the temple mandapam. The temple is also associated with Gajendra Moksham: the Gajendra Pushkarani tank lies in front of the temple, and Peyalvar is said to have been blessed with a vision of Gajendra Moksham here. The consort is Alamelumangai, and this is noted as the only Vishnu temple with a mangalasasanam dedicated exclusively to the mother. Glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham by Pey Alvar and Tirumangai Alvar; Vedanta Desika composed the Ashtabhujashtakam here. town_description: Kancheepuram (Kanchipuram), about 75 km southwest of Chennai, is one of India's seven sacred cities and is famed as the 'city of a thousand temples', home to 15 Divya Desams, the Shaivite Ekambaranathar and Kamakshi Amman temples, and its renowned handloom silk sarees.

travel.airport: Chennai International Airport (MAA), about 75 km away, is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Kanchipuram railway station on the Chengalpattu-Arakkonam line.
travel.road: On the Chennai-Bangalore highway (NH-48) corridor via Chennai-Chengalpattu; the temple is in Chinna Kanchipuram (listed by some sources as Reddypet), about 2 km from the Varadaraja Perumal Temple - reachable by auto or taxi within town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Aadi (July-August) for the Gajendra Moksha festival.
